question: Distinguish between a composite supply and a mixed supply under the CGST Act, 2017 and explain how the tax liability on each is determined.

points.label: Composite supply
points.description: A supply by a taxable person to a recipient of two or more taxable supplies of goods or services or both which are naturally bundled and supplied together in the ordinary course of business, one of which is the principal supply.

points.label: Principal supply
points.description: The main element of a composite supply, to which the other supplies are only ancillary; for example, when goods are sold with packing, transport and insurance, the goods are the principal supply.

points.label: Mixed supply
points.description: Two or more individual supplies of goods or services made together for a single price, where the combination is not a composite supply; for example, a festive hamper of soft drinks, chocolates and a toy sold for one price.

points.label: Tax treatment
points.description: A composite supply is treated as a supply of the principal supply; a mixed supply is treated as a supply of the item in it that attracts the highest rate of tax.

points.label: Test of natural bundling
points.description: Whether items are naturally bundled depends on whether they are normally supplied together in that trade, how customers see the package, whether a single price is charged, and whether the items are usually available separately; items that are normally sold separately and are simply grouped point to a mixed supply.
points.basis: CGST Act, 2017, section 2(30): meaning of 'naturally bundled' in the ordinary course of business
